doc.title: Dave Bennett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 16, 2025

title: Discovering Jerry Lee Lewis and learning rock and roll piano
summary: He first heard Jerry Lee Lewis at twelve on a Billboard set and learned the piano style by ear around age 23.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. I’m telling you, there’s nothing like [knocks on desk] on the piano doing Jerry Lee Lewis. That is just like a joy.

Well yeah, I remember I was twelve years old when I first heard his music. I bought this Billboard rock & roll set. It was 1957 through ’61 and I mean for pure enjoyment the ‘50s is just — I love that era. I love the music, I love the styles and but yeah, “Whole Lotta Shakin’” and “Great Balls of Fire” were on there. And I just remember number one it made me happy. It was just such a great sound, a great groove, a great pocket. And it wasn’t until my early twenties that I wanted to learn how to do that properly. I would dabble at a piano at school if they had one, and I could sound out a very elementary version of “Whole Lotta Shakin’ Going On” but I was about 23 and I got the bug again and I thought you know I want to learn this. So I just grabbed all the recordings of his I could and learned it by ear you know and now I’m doing it more.
